To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the relationship between student-teaching grades and post-training performance is weak and (b) student teachers who perform well during student teaching do not necessarily perform well in their first years of teaching.

(1) the relationship between student‐teaching grades and the post‐teaching performances is not strong; and (2) there is much divergence between student‐teachng grades and the post-teaching performances.
The student teaching grades of student teachers were not a reliable predictor of their post-training teaching performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between student‐training practices and the post‐ training performances of teachers in the Nigerian educational system.

student teaching grades do not seem to be valid predictors of post‐training performances, but they may be valid predictors of some aspects of the post‐training performance of teachers.
student teaching is a useful tool for the development of teaching skills, but not a very reliable indicator of teaching effectiveness.
